title: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR MANAGING EVENTS USING AN AVATAR BASED USER INTERFACE
technical_field: The following disclosure relates to a system and method for managing events using an avatar based user interface.
background_art:
[0002] Effective task management and reminders play a vital role in maintaining productivity and reducing stress. Many individuals struggle with staying organized and efficiently managing their tasks, often encountering issues such as forgetting important deadlines, neglecting appointments, and feeling overwhelmed due to a lack of structure. One common challenge is relying solely on memory to recall tasks, leading to forgetfulness and missed opportunities. Lacking a centralized system for tracking tasks can result in scattered information and overlooked items. Additionally, various appointments and events are often scheduled in different intervals (e.g., every three weeks vs. bi-weekly) which can cause subsequent days or weeks to look different and require different planning.
[0003] Another common challenge is keeping task management fun and interesting. Traditional task management systems, such as calendars, lack the efficiency and enjoyment brought by visual effects. Without these captivating visual cues, the interface can become uninteresting and less engaging, potentially resulting in reduced user interaction. This absence of visual distinction can lead to information overload, making it difficult for users to differentiate between various events and tasks on their calendars, especially when they are scheduled at different intervals. Moreover, the lack of visual effects complicates the process of prioritizing tasks and events, potentially causing users to miss deadlines or forget appointments. The intuitiveness of traditional task management applications suffers as users may struggle to navigate and comprehend the interface without visual cues, particularly affecting users with diverse learning styles and accessibility requirements. Furthermore, without visual effects, the emotional connection between users and the traditional application weakens, as visual effects often evoke emotions and create a more personalized experience.

The body part of the avatar may correspond to the body part of the user. The at least one processor may be also configured to generate a reminder for the user based on the event information associated to the body part of the avatar.

detailed_description:
[0041] An object of the present disclosure is to help a user stay organized by taking away the tedious work component of setting up tasks, appointments, and tracking timelines (as well as anticipate upcoming appointments) in traditional task management applications, and instead, make managing events more fun and engaging.
[0042] Another object of the present disclosure is to assist users in tracking appointments and tasks related to their body, while eliminating any negative connotations or need for secrecy. The goal is to promote the idea that seeking appointments for enhancing one's appearance and well-being is a normal and positive aspect of maintaining happiness and health.
[0043] Therefore, the disclosed embodiments relate to a system and method for managing events using an avatar based user interface. The disclosed system manages events relating to a user's body using a graphical user interface (GUI). For instance, an avatar is used as a visual representation of the user's body. The avatar may be configured to any shape of the user's body to help the user be comfortable with his/her/their appearance without any outside influence. The user's event information (e.g., event data) is associated with a body part of the avatar. A reminder is created for the user based on the event information associated with the body part of the avatar.

[0066] In one embodiment, the documents of the database 107 may be structured with a pre-defined data model or format. In another embodiment, the documents of the database 107 may be unstructured. In yet another embodiment, the database 107 may contain both structured and unstructured documents. Structured data is data in a defined format, or code, that makes it easily readable and/or searchable by a computer. Examples of structured data include JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), Extensible Markup Language (XML) formatted files, YAML Ain't Markup Language (YAML) and fixed width/field file formats. Unstructured data is not structured with pre-defined data models or schema. Examples of unstructured data may include the content of documents, journals, books, health records, metadata, audio, video, analog data, images, files, and unstructured text such as the body of an e-mail message, Web page, or word-processor document. Besides the difference between how structured or unstructured data is stored in a relational database versus stored outside of one, the biggest difference is the ease of analyzing structured data versus unstructured data. Mature analytics tools exist for structured data, but analytics tools for mining unstructured data may be emerging and developing. Dealing with unstructured data is important, since a vast majority (i.e., 80% or higher) of all potentially usable business information may originate in unstructured form.
[0067] It will be appreciated that the database 107 may be stored in a memory 105 or other non-transitory medium coupled with the system 102 and may be implemented by a plurality of databases, each of which stores a portion of the information. The database 107 is structured with a pre-defined data model or format, such as a relational database having a relational model of data. The database 107 includes a plurality of data items, or entities, stored in association with one or more properties. Each property is associated with a value. The relation from an item to a property is a one too many, with each of the latter having an associated value. In a Relational Database Management System (RDBMS), which is a software system used to maintain relational databases, an item is a row and a property is a related value of the item in a column. Stated another way, a property is an entity's data value, or the data instances themselves. A name space may be incorporated into the name of a property since there is no hierarchy to them. For example, the property "user.age" could represent a column "age" in a "user" table found in an RDBMS.

[0136] Furthermore, the operation for system 102 may include assigning a priority level to the generated reminder based on a deadline of the reminder or a level of importance (Block 316). [0137] One example of a criterium for determining the priority level of a reminder is its deadline. In other words, how soon a particular reminder needs to be acted upon or completed is a crucial factor. Reminders with closer deadlines are assigned higher priority levels, signifying that they require immediate attention or action. For example, the processor 103 determines a priority level based on the time before a deadline is reached. The closer a deadline approaches for an event, the higher the priority level is assigned to the event. A priority level may range from 0 to 5 with 5 being the highest or most urgent priority level.
[0138] The level of importance of a reminder is another example of a criterium of consideration for priority assignment. Not all reminders are of equal significance. Some tasks or events may be more critical than others. For example, a reminder for hormone therapy might be deemed more important than a reminder for a haircut appointment. The level of importance for each body part or event type is input by the user in the input section 802. The user may assign the level of importance in a range between 0 to 5 with 5 being the highest or most important. The above described criteria for determining a priority level of a reminder are examples and any number of other criteria may be used to determine a priority level.
[0139] To determine an overall priority level for a body part or event type associated with a body part, the processor 103 determines the average between the priority level assigned to a deadline and the priority level assigned to a level of importance. The overall priority level is then assigned to the corresponding body part and/or input event type. In another example, a separate priority level is assigned for each. In other words, a reminder for an event corresponding to a body part may be assigned one priority level based on corresponding deadlines alone and another priority level based on level of importance alone. In one example, the user may be able to select which priority level takes precedence. In another example, both priority levels remain associated with the reminder corresponding to the body part.
[0140] Thus, each reminder is assigned a priority level (or one or more priority levels) based on the deadline and/or level of importance. By assigning priority levels to these reminders, the system 102 can advantageously help users focus their attention on the most time-sensitive and critical matters.
[0141] The operation for system 102 may further include modifying the appearance of the at least one body part of the avatar associated with the reminder based on the assigned priority level (Block 318). In other words, the system 102 may provide visual cues for body parts of the avatar associated with a priority level for their reminders. Therefore, the system 102 has the capability to visually distinguish body parts of the avatar associated with different priority levels for their respective reminders. In this regard, the system 102 may create a "heat map," which is a representation of data in the form of a map or diagram in which data values (priority levels in this example) are represented as colors, shades of black/grey/white, or other varying patterns and the like to distinguish values from one another.
[0142] FIG. 12 illustrates a screenshot 1200, which includes the avatar having body parts assigned to different priority levels, of a mobile device in accordance with an embodiment of the disclosed system. Referring to FIG. 12, the avatar 504 is depicted as having both its head and legs assigned a priority level. In this example, different colors or shadings are used to differentiate the different priority levels. Other indicators may be used, such as numerical call outs for each body part assigned a priority level, outlining the body parts, and the like. In other words, FIG. 12 illustrates a heat map where at least one body part, assigned a priority level, is represented by a distinct color or shade, effectively conveying the level of importance to the user. In one example, a darker color or shade may be indicative of a higher priority level.
[0143] For example, the system 102 receives event information concerning the user's head and legs (or at least a portion of the legs). Subsequently, the system 102 associates the event information related to the user's head with the avatar's head and associates the event information concerning the user's legs with the avatar's legs. The event information concerning the user's head is deemed to hold significant importance due to the context of a nose surgery, while the event information concerning the user's legs holds lower importance, as it pertains to a waxing treatment. A first reminder based on the event information associated with the avatar's head is generated, and a second reminder based on the event information tied to the avatar's legs is generated. Consequently, the avatar's head is granted a high-priority status in accordance with the level of importance, while the avatar's legs are assigned a low-priority status. To visually convey this prioritization, alterations are made to the avatar's appearance, as illustrated in FIG. 12. Specifically, the avatar's head adopts a darker coloration to signal to the user that the reminder associated with the head carries a higher priority level than the reminder linked to the legs.
[0144] Another example may relate to multiple reminders being assigned priority levels based on their deadlines. For instance, when faced with multiple reminders scheduled for the same day, the system's processor 103 compares the overall priority levels of each reminder, ensuring a streamlined display for the user. For instance, if a nose surgery reminder is designated a priority level of 5, surpassing a manicure reminder with a level 4 priority, the system employs a visual differentiation by displaying the reminders in different colors. This intuitive approach enables users to readily discern the varying urgency or importance of tasks. Furthermore, in cases where multiple reminders share the same highest priority level, the system maintains clarity by presenting them with a consistent pattern or color associated with that priority level, facilitating quick recognition of tasks of equal significance.
[0145] This dynamic prioritization ensures that urgent or time-critical tasks receive the user's immediate attention, while tasks with more flexible timelines are acknowledged but do not disrupt the user's focus on immediate, pressing matters.
[0146] In another example, when multiple reminders are linked to the same body part, a numerical badge may be shown next to or associated with the body part. This badge indicates the number of reminders or scheduled events associated with that specific body part. For example, if a separate event/reminder is associated with the eyes, nose, and mouth of the avatar, a numerical badge in the form of a small bubble, for example, may be displayed next to the head of the avatar with a number "3" to indicate that three events/reminders pertain to the head of the avatar. As described above, a user may select the head and zoom-in on the head to then either further select subparts of the head, such as the eyes, nose, or mouth, to see the different events/reminders associated with those body parts.
[0147] In another embodiment, the system 102 may employ various visual cues and alerts to communicate these priority levels effectively. High-priority reminders may trigger more noticeable alerts, such as popup notifications, vibrant colors, or sound cues, to capture the user's attention promptly. In contrast, low-priority reminders may employ subtler visual indications, like muted colors or smaller notification icons, signaling their lower urgency without causing unnecessary distraction.
[0148] By adapting the avatar's appearance and employing these intelligent priority assignments, the system 102 enhances the user's experience by providing clear, context-aware cues that aid in managing and prioritizing tasks efficiently as it relates the avatar to the user's own body. This ensures that the user remains in control of their schedule and can address their commitments effectively, whether they involve significant events like medical appointments or less critical tasks like personal grooming appointments.
[0149] The operation may also include storing a user's personalized avatar under the user profile in the database 107. The user profile includes the personalized avatar having the generated reminders associated to at least one body part of the avatar. Storing the user's avatar under the user's profile preserves the avatar's appearance, associated reminders, and also ensures that the user's customization and preferences are readily accessible for future interactions.
[0150] Additionally, the operation may transmit or share the user's profile to another user (Block 320), such as to enable collaboration between each user. By allowing the user to share their personalized avatar with other users, the system 102 advantageously allows users to coordinate and share events. Furthermore, users going through similar events may be able to come together to help each other through obstacles by sharing their avatars as an outline or template for guidance and inspiration. For example, a user's avatar can serve as a source of inspiration, showing what is achievable and offering a clear path forward. Users can replicate successful approaches and adapt them to their own circumstances.
